name: 3D Solids
miniText: How can a two-dimensional display communicate three-dimensional shape? NetLogo 3D Solids samples points on selected solid surfaces, stores spherical coordinates, rotates them by changing an angle, and projects their positions into the view. Brightness supplies an additional depth cue. The graphics methods in [1], differential geometry in [2], and computational geometry in [3] provide complementary foundations for separating a surface, its parameterization, and its displayed approximation. The model illustrates coordinate conversion and rotation rather than physical motion of a rigid material. Its random point cloud is finite, the display omits a full optical rendering pipeline, and visual smoothness depends on sampling. Recognizing a convincing sphere or cube therefore demonstrates a useful representation, without proving uniform surface sampling or geometric accuracy of every generated point.
